detailed_rationale:
OneSource Specialty Pharma is a recently-listed biologics CDMO (contract development and manufacturing, injectable biologics), demerged out of Strides Pharma. The headline growth number in our quant data (231% 3-year revenue CAGR) is a demerger/listing base-effect artifact from a tiny pre-listing comparison base and should not be read as organic growth -- we flag this explicitly rather than credit it, consistent with our guidance on merger/demerger distortions. The real, current picture is far less flattering: FY26 revenue was Rs 1,422 Cr, down slightly (-1.6%) from FY25's Rs 1,445 Cr, with a full-year net loss of Rs 74 Cr. Quarterly results have been genuinely volatile -- in Q3 FY26 (Dec 2025), the business posted an Rs 89 Cr loss on just Rs 290 Cr revenue at a 6% margin, before partial recovery to Rs 25 Cr profit in the June 2026 quarter.

Two items concern us beyond the operating volatility. First, debt has nearly doubled year-on-year (Rs 772 Cr to Rs 1,504 Cr) at a business that is not yet reliably profitable. Second, and more materially, 37.2% of promoter holding is currently pledged, alongside a reduction in promoter stake from 34.25% to 30.48% -- a pledge of that size at a loss-making, newly-listed company is a genuine balance-sheet and governance flag, not a stale-data artifact. A recent change in the Global Head role (July 2026) adds to near-term management-continuity uncertainty.

The CDMO-biologics industry backdrop is a real, structural tailwind (Western pharma diversifying manufacturing away from China, biologics outsourcing growing), and this is the kind of business that can look unprofitable while capacity is being built and qualified -- but we need to see the losses narrow and the pledge come down before treating the long-term industry thesis as sufficient reason to look past the current numbers.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, following the quant score -- a business that is currently loss-making, carries rapidly rising debt, and has more than a third of promoter shares pledged does not clear the bar for a rescue to Hold; the long-term CDMO-biologics thesis is real, but the balance-sheet and governance signals here are the more urgent, near-term facts, and we are not overriding the quant Sell.
summary: OneSource Specialty Pharma is a biologics contract manufacturer spun off from Strides Pharma. Despite a headline growth figure inflated by the spin-off's small starting base, actual FY26 revenue was roughly flat and the company posted a net loss for the year, with a particularly weak December-2025 quarter. Debt has nearly doubled over the past year, and more than a third of promoter shares are currently pledged. We rate it a Sell: the long-term contract-manufacturing growth story may prove out over time, but the current financial and governance picture does not support a Hold today.
positive_para: OneSource operates in a genuine structural growth industry -- biologics CDMO/outsourcing, benefiting from Western pharma's push to diversify manufacturing away from China -- and Q1 FY27 showed a partial return to profitability (Rs 25 Cr) after the Q3 FY26 loss, which could mark the start of capacity utilization improving as newer facilities ramp.
negative_para: The headline '231% 3-year revenue growth' in our data is a spin-off base-effect artifact, not real organic growth -- actual FY26 revenue was essentially flat, and the company posted a genuine net loss for the year with one quarter's loss (Rs 89 Cr) larger than a full quarter's revenue base a year earlier would have supported. Debt nearly doubled in a single year at a business not yet consistently profitable, and 37.2% of promoter shares are pledged -- a meaningful governance and balance-sheet risk signal that should not be waved through as 'just newly listed.'
reverse_dcf_judgment: With negative trailing earnings, a conventional PE is meaningless; the stock is effectively priced on a multi-year narrative that capacity being built today will convert into durable, profitable biologics CDMO revenue. That narrative may well prove correct given the industry backdrop, but a near-40% promoter pledge and rapidly rising debt are the kind of facts that should be resolved before extending that narrative the benefit of the doubt at the current price.
